Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.
2. The applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 741 of 2021, under Sections 376, 120B IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012, P.S. Handia, District Prayagraj, during pendency of the trial.

3. An FIR has been lodged to the effect that on 10.12.2021 at about 4.0p.m. sister of the informant aged about 17 years had gone to market to purchase clothes and thereafter she went missing and on extensive search, her whereabouts could not be known.

1 4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further contended that initially an FIR under Section 363 IPC against unknown person.
It is further contended that applicant has been granted bail under Sections 363, 366 IPC and Section 7/8 of POCSO Act.
It is further contended that subsequent to the investigation Section 376, 120-B IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act was added.
It is further contended that the victim was medically examined in which she has refused her internal examination.
It is further submitted that as per x-ray report, victim was found above 18 years and below 20 years.
It is further submitted that there are major contradictions in the statements of the victim said to have been recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
It is further submitted that victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
There is no evidence of forceful assault.
It is further submitted that the victim has been falsely shown as minor only to aggravate the offence and cause the imprisonment of the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act.
The victim is infact a major.
The applicant is in jail since 03.01.2024 and has no criminal history.
Charge-sheet has been filed and conclusion of trial will take time, hence it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

5. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant by contending that the applicant is absconding and is not cooperating in trial.

It is further submitted that the charge sheet in the matter has been submitted way back on 27.7.2022 and still charge have not been framed and is deliberately delaying the trial and in case he is allowed bail there is possibility of tampering with the evidence by him.
6.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment as well as totality of facts and circumstances, at this stage without commenting on the merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
However, any observation made herein-above, will not affect the trial of the case.

7. Let the applicant- Vinay Kumar Dubey @ Pradumn Dubey, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
Vinay Kumar Dubey @ Pradumn Dubey vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89497103/
2 then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A IPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial within a period of one year after the release of the applicant.
8.
In case of breach of of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

9. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
